questions.stem: Which of the following is a correct statement about the atomic theory proposed by John Dalton
choices: It explained the results of many experiments very successfully
It was the first theory to suggest that atoms are divisible
It failed to explain the law of conservation of mass
It was able to explain the existence of sub-atomic particles
questions.solution: Dalton's atomic theory successfully explained many experimental results, including the laws of conservation of mass, constant composition, and multiple proportions. The claim that it was the first to suggest atoms are divisible is incorrect, as Dalton believed atoms were indivisible. The idea that it failed to explain the law of conservation of mass is false, as it did explain it. The theory also did not account for sub-atomic particles, which were discovered later.

questions.stem: According to Hund’s rule of maximum multiplicity, when do electrons start pairing in orbitals of the same subshell?
choices: When all orbitals are filled with one electron each
When the subshell has more than three orbitals
When the subshell is completely filled with electrons
When the subshell has more than four orbitals
questions.solution: The correct answer is when all orbitals are filled with one electron each. Hund’s rule states that electrons will occupy separate orbitals with parallel spins before pairing occurs. The other options are incorrect because they do not align with the principle that pairing begins only after each orbital has one electron.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a noble gas?
choices: Na
K
Mg
Ar
questions.solution: Argon (Ar) is a noble gas because it has a full outer electron shell, making it chemically inert. Sodium (Na) and potassium (K) are reactive metals that readily lose electrons, and magnesium (Mg) is a metal that typically loses two electrons. Therefore, Ar is the correct answer.

hi.critique: Translation is accurate, technical terms match Indian curriculum, and the question structure is preserved.

questions.stem: What did Rutherford's experiment reveal about the structure of the atom?
choices: The atom is mostly empty space
The nucleus contains electrons
The electrons are distributed uniformly
The positive charge is spread throughout the atom
questions.solution: The correct answer is that the atom is mostly empty space. Rutherford's experiment showed that most alpha particles passed through the gold foil without deflection, suggesting that atoms have a lot of empty space. The other options are incorrect because electrons are not in the nucleus, and the positive charge is concentrated in a small area, not spread throughout the atom.

questions.stem: How many electrons in an atom can have the quantum numbers n = 3, l = 0?
questions.solution: For n = 3 and l = 0, we are referring to the 3s subshell, which can hold a maximum of 2 electrons. The other options represent the capacities of different subshells, not the 3s subshell.

hi.stem: किसी परमाणु में कितने इलेक्ट्रॉन ऐसे हो सकते हैं जिनके क्वांटम संख्याएँ n = 3, l = 0 हैं?
hi.solution: n = 3 और l = 0 के लिए हम 3s उपकोश के बारे में बात कर रहे हैं, जो अधिकतम 2 इलेक्ट्रॉन धारण कर सकता है। अन्य विकल्प विभिन्न उपकोशों की क्षमताओं का प्रतिनिधित्व करते हैं, 3s उपकोश की नहीं।
hi.critique: Translation is accurate, maintains the original meaning, and uses standard Hindi terminology for quantum numbers and subshells.

questions.stem: If a cathode ray tube is coated with a material that glows when struck by cathode rays, what would happen if the material is replaced with one that does not glow
choices: The cathode rays would stop moving
The cathode rays would change direction
No bright spot would be observed
The cathode rays would become visible
questions.solution: The cathode rays themselves are not visible, so if the material that glows when struck by them is replaced with one that does not, no bright spot would be observed. Cathode rays would still move and travel in the same direction, and they would not become visible just because the coating changes. The other options incorrectly assume the rays themselves change behavior or become visible without a glowing material.

hi.solution: कैथोड किरणें स्वयं दृश्यमान नहीं होती हैं, इसलिए यदि उस पदार्थ को जो कैथोड किरणों द्वारा टक्कर खाने पर चमकता है, को ऐसे पदार्थ से बदल दिया जाए जो चमकता नहीं है, तो कोई चमकदार धब्बा दिखाई नहीं देगा। कैथोड किरणें अभी भी गति करेंगी और उसी दिशा में यात्रा करेंगी, और उन्हें उस लेप के कारण दृश्यमान नहीं हो जाएगा। अन्य विकल्प गलत तरीके से किरणों के व्यवहार में परिवर्तन या दृश्यमान होने की कल्पना करते हैं बिना किसी चमकदार पदार्थ के।

mr.stem: जर कॅथोड किरण नलिकेच्या सतहला एखाद्या सामग्रीने झाकले जाते जे कॅथोड किरणांनी टीका केल्याने जळते, तर जर ती सामग्री एखाद्या सामग्रीने बदलली जाते जे कॅथोड किरणांनी टीका केल्याने जळत नाही, तर काय होईल?
choices: कॅथोड किरण थांबले जातील
कॅथोड किरण दिशा बदलतील
कोणताही उजळ बिंदू न दिसेल
कॅथोड किरण दिसू लागतील
mr.solution: कॅथोड किरण स्वतः दृश्य नसतात, म्हणून जर ज्या सामग्रीने कॅथोड किरणांनी टीका केल्याने जळते ती सामग्री बदलून ज्याने जळत नाही ती बदलली जाते, तर कोणताही उजळ बिंदू दिसणार नाही. कॅथोड किरण अजूनही चालतील आणि त्यांची दिशा बदलणार नाही, आणि जरी लेप बदलला गेला तरी ते स्वतः दृश्य होऊ शकत नाहीत. इतर विकल्प चुकीच्या पद्धतीने किरणांच्या वर्तनाचा किंवा दृश्यतेचा अंदाज घेतात.

questions.stem: If the momentum of an electron is given as h/4π × 0.05 nm, is there a problem in defining this value?
choices: Yes, because momentum cannot be defined precisely
No, because the value is within the uncertainty principle
Yes, because it violates the Heisenberg uncertainty principle
No, because it is a valid value for momentum
questions.solution: The Heisenberg uncertainty principle states that the product of uncertainty in position and momentum must be at least h/4π. If the momentum is given as h/4π × 0.05 nm, it violates this principle. The third option is correct. The first option is incorrect because it misrepresents the uncertainty principle. The second and fourth options are incorrect because they fail to account for the principle's implications.

hi.stem: यदि इलेक्ट्रॉन के संवेग को h/4π × 0.05 nm के रूप में दिया गया है, तो इस मान को परिभाषित करने में कोई समस्या है क्या?
choices: हाँ, क्योंकि संवेग को सटीक रूप से परिभाषित नहीं किया जा सकता

नहीं, क्योंकि यह संवेग के लिए एक वैध मान है
hi.solution: हाइजेनबर्ग अनिश्चितता सिद्धांत कहता है कि स्थिति और संवेग में अनिश्चितता का गुणनफल कम से कम h/4π होना चाहिए। यदि संवेग को h/4π × 0.05 nm के रूप में दिया गया है, तो इस सिद्धांत का उल्लंघन होता है। तीसरा विकल्प सही है। पहला विकल्प अनिश्चितता सिद्धांत के गलत अर्थ के कारण गलत है। दूसरा और चौथा विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि वे सिद्धांत के अनुप्रयोग को ध्यान में नहीं रखते।

mr.stem: जर इलेक्ट्रॉनच्या वेगवेगाचे मूल्य h/4π × 0.05 nm दिले गेले असेल, तर हे मूल्य निश्चित करण्यात काही समस्या असेल का?
